properties.decision:
Recorded as brainstorming on 2026-09-20 from flo2 F26, not as a proposal. The three shapes and the per-client mechanism already exist; this is only about the FALLBACK.

THE BIND, stated exactly by the reporter: you cannot simultaneously keep the text block non-empty AND have an empty-fallback client read the structured object. The signpost exists to avoid SILENCE for a client reading the wrong field (req:never-silently-absent); an empty block is the only thing that reaches a client which falls back only on emptiness. Both cannot hold.

OPTIONS.
(a) DEFAULT TO DUPLICATE — the serialized payload in the text block, the spec's own worked shape. Serves every population without knowing anything about the client. COUNTER, and it is the measured one: fact:every-reply-was-sent-twice removed exactly this because it is a flat 2× on the wire, and it is why three rollups were refused by harnesses. reflow2's replies are large — the reporter measured describe_schema at 53,108 characters before trimming. Making this the default resurrects the cost for every unknown client.
(b) DEFAULT TO EMPTY. Cheapest, serves the text-first population, and loses the signpost's protection: a client reading only `content` gets silence, which req:never-silently-absent says is indistinguishable from reflow2 never having been configured.
(c) PER-TOOL RATHER THAN GLOBAL, the reporter's own suggestion: the handful of tools a constrained client actually calls get the payload in the text; the bulk keep the signpost. Their measured dependency is twelve tools. Bounds the doubling to small replies and leaves the large rollups alone — which is the shape of the cost.
(d) KEEP THE SIGNPOST AND ADD CLIENTS BY NAME as they are measured. The status quo. COUNTER: a name-keyed policy cannot learn, and every connector is unknown at the moment it first connects, which is the moment that matters.

⚠️ WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT AND HAS NOT BEEN MEASURED: whether any client injects BOTH representations into the model's context. The reporter is careful here — the doubling is wire bytes, and a client normally picks one representation, so the cost lands on a pipe rather than the context budget reflow2 guards with budget_chars. Nobody has checked whether a client exists that injects both. That measurement decides how bad (a) and (c) actually are.

⭐ AND ONE CHEAP THING IS TRUE UNDER EVERY OPTION: the placeholder is the only shape wrong for every reader, so moving off it does not depend on choosing between these.
properties.name: OPEN — what should the reply shape default to for a client nobody has measured, now that every new connector is one?
